dct_description_sm: The Yellowknives Dene have already began to feel the impacts of climate change. Permafrost degradation and drinking water are the main concern of this project. In the past 6 months, the Yellowknives Dene First Nation (YKDFN) has been working on a climate change plan which includes a recommendation to better understanding permafrost in the Dettah Road area. Currently, the permafrost has lost some of its thickness and this may negatively impact some of the First Nation's infrastructure.   The winter ice road is important for its use to save travel time and reduce transportation costs between Dettah, Ndilo and Yellowknife. Other factor such as housing and historical importance make the road an important part of YKDFN and necessitates a land-use plan. Another emerging concern is the water. The pump in Yellowknife is to be closed down as a result of mainly erosion. If funding is not made available, this leaves the Yellowknives Dene to start taking water from the Yellowknife Bay, which has arsenic contamination from the mines.
